independent_reconstruction: Reconstruct fixed-step native FFN as v_t=Q1(smooth1(modulate(norm2(r_t)))), z_t=A v_t+b1, a_{t,g}=Q2_g(smooth2(GELU_tanh(z_{t,g}))) for original ordered 64-wide groups, and F_t=b2+Σ_g B_g a_{t,g}; final current-token gate and residual are applied downstream. The archived HiF4 GPU path hifx_quant_cuda_inner loops over exactly 64 channel positions per group, with a 64/8/4 nested scale hierarchy, and R12 preserves full ordered64 group and row separability; this is enough to treat each Q2_g as a group-local mapping for the audited configuration. If the output operand a_{t,g} exactly matches a_{a,g} for all g in common set S, then Σ_{g∈S} B_g a_{t,g}=Σ_{g∈S} B_g a_{a,g} in mathematical decoded arithmetic. Thus computing this shared contribution once per tile and computing g∉S per token is exact at the mathematical operator level; current-token gate/residual must remain separate. It is not the same as copying full FFN rows or fitting a dense correction. Anchoring and S selection must be causally before the skipped target W1 rows.
decisive_argument: SUPPORT the exact conditional group-reuse identity and its explicit T-token MAC accounting, not its measured applicability. Let m=13824,d=5120,T tile tokens,b=64|S| shared hidden coordinates. Dense two-matmul cost 2Tdm; the anchor-once shared-subspace representation costs 2d[b+T(m−b)], so mathematical saving fraction (b/m)(1−1/T). If the token W1 was already computed before recognizing Q2 equality, only W2 part may be shared, halving this theoretical saving. This is a genuinely different causal output-preserving operator from past whole-row reuse, and the saved R13 common-row bound cannot be transferred. The proof remains valid on any format whose Q2 state is block-separable on the chosen groups; HiF4 64-wide is source-grounded but MXFP4/NVFP4 require their own scale-aligned partitions.
counterexample_or_discriminator: CRITICAL format/ordering discriminator: The repo's tools/packed_ffn_reference.py has an optional gain applied AFTER Q2 and cast back to input dtype BEFORE W2: v2=BF16(Q2(...)*alpha_t). If alpha differs between tile rows, equality of raw Q2_g output does NOT imply equality of the actual W2 input. For one nonzero a_g with alpha_anchor=1 and alpha_target=2, W2_g a_g and W2_g (2 a_g) differ even though a_g matches. Therefore the sufficient equality MUST be on the final post-Q2, post-gain, post-cast W2 operand actually consumed, or else alpha is proven constant/commuted under a separately verified numerical contract. This is a source-specific missing condition, not a disproof of the group-reuse family. Geometric discriminator: A_g is 64×5120, so null(A_g) has dimension at least 5056. There exist arbitrarily large ||Δv||∞ with A_gΔv=0 and exact preactivation equality, whereas original κ_g||Δv||∞ may be arbitrarily large. The proposed infinity-distance certificate may therefore reject many truly identical groups. A stronger causal row-space/sketch certificate can exploit a low-rank U with ||A_gΔv||∞≤ max_j ||a_jU||₂·||UᵀΔv||₂ + max_j||a_j(I−UUᵀ)||₂·||(I−UUᵀ)Δv||₂, while charging cost of UᵀΔv and residual norms. The special case Δv∈null(A_g) is a mathematical separator, not a claim that native Wan tokens concentrate there.
constructive_revision: Maintain SUPPORT for the scoped conditional theorem. In a next proposal revision, explicitly define a_{t,g}^{W2} as the entire effective W2 operand AFTER any per-row gain, BF16 conversion, and other native pre-W2 transformations. The sharing condition should become a_{t,g}^{W2}=a_{anchor,g}^{W2}; when scalar gain differs and exact decoded arithmetic allows, discuss separately a cached canonical group contribution followed by per-row scale, but do not claim bitwise equality through BF16 cast/reordered GEMM. Formally compare original infinity-norm certificate versus a shared low-rank/dual-norm certificate with costs: shared U projection O(Tdr), per-group residual data and summations, anchor W1, scale-state and output-tile packing. For the native 64/8/4 HiF4 hierarchy, a full-cell µ threshold can be conservative but must include scale/rounding boundaries. The post-Q2-gain counterexample should be resolved without requiring dense restoration, R256, or experiments. On MXFP4/NVFP4, choose the compatible block scale partition and explicitly handle NV tensor-global scale if it couples groups. Do not update the original v1 file; record any change as v2 and invite a different agent to check it.
